findings: Replay v114 adds the R32 integer vertex formats already accepted by the UMD and reaches the provider work rejection.

The old admission estimate multiplies full scissor area by all 70 triangles. The selected device now computes bounds first, then a complete tile plan is checked against the unchanged 4096-tile limit before coverage or destination modification.
The captured Start menu draw executes on the physical NPU with 2077 covered samples. Both replays match the independent scalar pixel oracle exactly, and final pixels hash-identically to CPU replay.
Contract checks admit exactly 4096 planned tiles, reject an excess, reject invalid bounds, and verify a 70-triangle sparse draw that the old scissor estimate rejected.
The first v115 build failed because Windows defines small as a macro; the diagnostic variable was renamed. v115a is an incremental diagnostic build. v116 is the separately qualified clean build.
These are isolated draw and contract checks; no usable desktop or performance benefit is established.
